title: Painted faces, boundary and hidden cubes
transcript: When you paint the outside of a cube block, the small pieces get different numbers of painted faces. Their position tells you how many. Check the corners, edges, face interiors and hidden cells. If one surface is unpainted, the old category counts can change.

An AMC practice problem can describe a painted cube before it is split. Count the unit cubes after splitting, using the original outside surface. In a Rossmoyne style extension, a different set of faces may be painted. Split the solid into layers where the rule is consistent.
A solid cube built from four by four by four unit cubes has all six big faces painted. How many unit cubes have three painted faces? Find the positions where three outside faces touch.
A corner touches three of the large faces. Along the interior of an edge a cube touches only two. There are four corner cubes on the top layer and four on the bottom layer. There are eight in all.
Paint all six faces of a solid five by four by four cuboid. How many small cubes have exactly two faces painted? A corner touches three large faces. Remove the corners from the edge counts.

There are four edges of each length. The edges of lengths five, four and four have three, two and two cubes between their endpoints. Multiply the sum of these three counts by four. This gives twenty-eight cubes with exactly two painted faces.

A cuboid is six unit cubes wide, five deep and four high. Paint the four vertical sides and the bottom. Leave the top unpainted. How many pieces have exactly two painted faces after splitting it into unit cubes?

The bottom layer already supplies one painted face. Exactly two requires one more, so count the bottom edge positions excluding its four corners. Every layer above the bottom has painted vertical faces only. The four corner positions of each layer touch two side faces. The top layer follows this same rule. Add the bottom and upper layer counts. There are twenty-six cubes with exactly two painted faces.

On the bottom map, the corners have three, sides between corners have two, and the interior has one. Above that layer, remove the bottom contribution from the same positions. This checks the classification covers every unit cube. No inner cell on an upper layer reaches a painted side.

A corner of an entirely painted block touches three faces. Subtract the endpoints before counting edge positions with exactly two. An unpainted face adds zero to a cube's painted-face count. A top corner may then have two painted faces rather than three.

List which outside faces are painted, and draw a footprint if the solid is hard to see. Include hidden edges in your count. Group cells that touch the same number of paint surfaces. Add the groups that match exactly what the question asks for.
